channel.title: NewsCenter — Top 5 news of the day — 2026-11-07
channel.description: The five news that matter most today, chosen from Laurent's newsletters. 164 news received.

item.title: 1. AI Stocks Fall After the U.S. Elections
item.description: Why it matters: The 5.5% Nasdaq drop and sharp declines in AI-related stocks signal that election-driven resistance to data-center expansion could materially raise infrastructure costs and slow the AI buildout. The Nasdaq fell 5.5%, while several chipmakers dropped more than 9% or by double digits. Wall Street fears a slowdown in data centers after the adoption of numerous local measures aimed at restricting them.

item.title: 2. Apple beats forecasts with record quarterly results
item.description: Why it matters: Apple’s record $114.5 billion quarter, above expectations, demonstrates continued strength in its core business and provides a major market benchmark for consumer technology demand. Apple generated 114.5 billion dollars in revenue in the fourth quarter of 2026, beating Wall Street forecasts and its previous quarterly record from the 2020 holiday season.

item.title: 3. OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber, specialized in exploit research
item.description: Why it matters: OpenAI’s launch of GPT-6 Cyber highlights the accelerating commercialization of AI for exploit research, raising both cybersecurity risks and competitive pressure on model providers. OpenAI is launching GPT-6 Cyber, with improved exploit research capabilities and a higher API price than Anthropic and Google.

item.title: 4. Beijing Blocks SoftBank’s Acquisition of ABB’s Robotics Division
item.description: Why it matters: China’s veto of SoftBank’s acquisition of ABB’s robotics division shows that industrial robotics is becoming a strategic asset subject to increasingly aggressive geopolitical controls. China vetoed SoftBank’s acquisition of ABB’s robotics division through its foreign investment oversight body. The decision highlights the growing strategic importance of industrial robots.

item.title: 5. Google will disable its AI services for students by default
item.description: Why it matters: Google’s decision to disable AI services for students by default at schools’ request shows how education customers and regulators are pushing vendors toward stricter controls on generative AI. Google plans to disable its AI services for students by default next year, at schools’ request. The measure will include Google Search, which is considered an AI product.
